- [USER] User inquired about the moral obligation of Catholics to donate to charity instead of spending money on luxury items.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant stated that in Catholic teachings, charity and giving to those in need are considered moral obligations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant referenced the Catechism of the Catholic Church, stating that "almsgiving, according to the Gospel, is not mere philanthropy. Rather it is a concrete expression of charity, a way of assisting in the immediate needs of our neighbors and showing solidarity with them" (2447).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explained that Catholic social teaching emphasizes caring for the poor and vulnerable and promoting the common good.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant noted that while there is no specific obligation to donate a certain amount of money or to avoid spending on luxury items, Catholics are called to use their resources and talents to promote the dignity of all human beings and work for the well-being of others.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant summarized that Catholics are encouraged to prioritize charity and the needs of others in their financial decisions and to use their resources in a way that promotes the common good.
